questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Borrowing and lifetime basics”?
options: Use rustup to keep toolchain updates and installed versions explicit.
A reference accesses a borrowed value without taking ownership.
Cargo is the main tool for creating, building, and testing projects.
Rust bindings are immutable unless declared mut.
questions.answer: A reference accesses a borrowed value without taking ownership.
questions.explanation:
A reference accesses a borrowed value without taking ownership.
Why: References let code access a value without taking ownership. Borrowing rules constrain simultaneous mutable and shared references; lifetime annotations describe relationships, not extend storage.

Borrowing provides references without moving ownership. You may have many immutable `&T` references or one active mutable `&mut T`; conflicting access is rejected to prevent data races. A reference cannot outlive its owner.
